# HMAC, HKDF and TLS 1.3 key-schedule vectors, one per line:
# `<name> | <kdf_driver.ls case> | <expected output in hex>`.
# Read by `crates/lex-sys/tests/conformance/kdf.rs`; `docs/hkdf.md` §4.
#
# Sources. RFC 4231 (HMAC-SHA256/384; test case 5, the truncated one, is
# not in the transcription), RFC 5869 A.1 to A.3, and a 1,200-byte HKDF
# output, from pyca/cryptography's `cryptography_vectors`. The TLS 1.3 key
# schedule from three places: RFC 8448 section 3 (the "Simple 1-RTT
# Handshake"), written down from the RFC and kept only where Python's
# hmac/hashlib reproduces the value from the trace's own inputs. The
# application traffic secrets and the exporter master secret did not
# reproduce as first written down, so they were left out; they are now
# taken from AWS s2n-tls's transcription of RFC 8448 section 3
# (`tests/unit/s2n_tls13_secrets_rfc8448_test.c`), whose every value
# reproduces in Python from its own inputs (`docs/hkdf.md` §4.2,
# `docs/tls-core.md` §6.1); NIST ACVP's TLS-v1.3-KDF-RFC8446 case, as Go's
# `crypto/tls` `TestACVPVectors` carries it (a PSK handshake: every
# secret, early to resumption); and OpenSSL's `test/tls13secretstest.c`
# (draft-ietf-tls-tls13-vectors-06, which OpenSSL's TLS 1.3 passes).
# Every line was checked against Python's hmac/hashlib before it was
# written here.
